# A query under a `for` whose fetch answers at once, so the query's instance,
# built at run time inside the page's first build, settles as it is made and
# its `@load` patches the page's label after the loop -- which the build has
# not made yet. fyne dereferenced the nil label, and gtk4 handed GTK a null
# widget. An instance's first settle is held until the page's build ends,
# as a component's own runs after its body.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func lookup(name string, life async.Lifetime) async.Result[int] {
    return {ok=name.length()}
}

component many ui.node {
    var total = 0

    ui.vbox {
        for var w = ["one", "three"] {
            async.query(on=w, fetch=lookup, @load(got) { total += got })
        }
        ui.text(value="{total}")
    }
}

func testEachAnswerCounts(t test.Test, c many) {
    t.wait(func() => c.total == 8, 5000)
    t.assert(c.total == 8)
}

ui.window {
    many()
}
